title: What is antardasha? Dasha sub-periods explained | Ask Tota
description: Antardasha is the sub-period inside a mahadasha. The order of the nine bhuktis, the one formula for their length, and how astrologers read the pair.
og_title: Antardasha, the chapter inside the chapter
og_description: Every mahadasha splits into nine antardashas in a fixed order. The formula for their length, a full worked table, and how astrologers read the pair.
h1: antardasha is the chapter inside the chapter
dek: a mahadasha sets the theme of years at a time. the antardasha is the planet that takes the microphone for a few months to a few years inside it. it follows a fixed order and a single formula, and it is usually where timing actually comes from.
card_title: antardasha is the chapter inside the chapter
card_dek: nine sub-periods inside every mahadasha, in a fixed order, sized by one formula. where vedic timing actually gets specific.
llms_desc: what an antardasha (bhukti) is in Vimshottari dasha, the order of the nine sub-periods, the formula for their length (mahadasha years times antardasha years divided by 120), a worked Saturn mahadasha table, and how the mahadasha and antardasha lords are read together.

faq.a: the sub-period inside a mahadasha. every mahadasha is divided into nine antardashas, one for each graha, in a fixed order. the mahadasha sets the overall theme and the antardasha lord colours a shorter stretch of it.

faq.q: what is the difference between mahadasha and antardasha?
faq.a: the mahadasha is the main period, from 6 to 20 years depending on the planet. the antardasha is a slice of it, from a few months to just over three years. astrologers read them as a pair.
multiply the mahadasha planet's years by the antardasha planet's years and divide by 120. so venus antardasha in saturn mahadasha is 19 times 20 divided by 120, about 3 years 2 months.

faq.q: what is the order of antardashas?
faq.a: the first antardasha belongs to the mahadasha lord itself. after that they follow the vimshottari order: ketu, venus, sun, moon, mars, rahu, jupiter, saturn, mercury, wrapping round until all nine have run.
another name for antardasha, common in south indian usage. the two words mean the same sub-period.

the third level down, a sub-period inside the antardasha, calculated with the same proportions. it can be a few days to a few months long, and some astrologers go further still to sookshma and prana dashas.

faq.q: which antardasha is the most important?
faq.a: there is no universal answer. it depends on what the antardasha planet owns and occupies in ur chart, and how it relates to the mahadasha lord. a friendly, well placed pair is usually read as smoother.

faq.q: why is the first antardasha the same planet as the mahadasha?
faq.a: because each mahadasha begins with its own lord's sub-period, sometimes written as saturn-saturn or venus-venus. it is the purest expression of that planet in the cycle.

faq.q: how do i find my current antardasha?
faq.a: u need ur birth date, time and place, so the moon's exact nakshatra position can be calculated. any vedic chart tool will list ur mahadasha, antardasha and their dates. ask tota shows them in the chart desk.

faq.q: can antardasha change my life suddenly?
faq.a: antardasha changes are where shifts are traditionally expected, because the planet in focus changes. in practice the change is usually a shift in themes over weeks rather than a switch flipped on a date.
sun antardasha inside sun mahadasha: 6 times 6 divided by 120, about 3 months 18 days.
venus antardasha inside venus mahadasha: 20 times 20 divided by 120, exactly 3 years 4 months.
